difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, integrality is equivalent to being affine and universally closed (source lines 9446-9455). The proof notes that in both cases the morphism is representable and that the conditions may be checked after base change by an affine scheme mapping into Y, invoking the locality statements for integrality, affineness and universal closedness, and then applies the corresponding equivalence for morphisms of schemes.
